note: Structured, sourced San Diego County electricity rate/provider data for the 'Find My System' calculator. Rates change - re-verify before relying on these for anything beyond a rough, clearly-labeled estimate. Web-search-derived figures below are NOT a substitute for the exact current SDG&E tariff PDF; treat as approximate pending direct tariff verification.
verification_status: approximate - derived from search-engine summaries of SDG&E's published rate tables and secondary sources, not a direct read of the tariff PDF. Re-verify against the source URLs below before publishing exact cents-per-kWh figures as fact.

delivery_utility.name: San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E)
delivery_utility.role: Delivers electricity to essentially all of San Diego County regardless of who supplies generation. Delivery charges apply whether a customer is bundled with SDG&E or enrolled in a CCA.

ccas.name: San Diego Community Power
ccas.type: Community Choice Aggregation (CCA) - generation only, SDG&E still delivers
ccas.note: Default PowerOn generation service reported at roughly 4% below SDG&E's comparable 2026 generation rate. Customers can opt out back to SDG&E generation at any time. Does not cover all San Diego County cities (e.g. not every incorporated city has joined).

touDr1.label: TOU-DR1
touDr1.effective: rates shown reflect the ~April 2026 SDG&E residential total-rate table window; SDG&E updates these multiple times per year
touDr1.baseline_credit_note: Applies to usage up to ~130% of baseline allocation; reduces effective rate across all periods.

peak_window_note: SDG&E's expensive period is late afternoon/evening (4-9pm summer, 5-8pm winter). Solar production is strongest mid-day, so a solar-only system mainly offsets electricity used while the sun is up, not the evening peak. A battery can shift some daytime production into the evening peak, but does not eliminate the peak - impact depends on battery capacity and continuous output limits, not just kWh stored.
